deliverables.title: Deliverable presence (Tier 1 gates)
deliverables.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Does proposal/report.pdf exist with substantive content (full sections, not a placeholder)?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check proposal/report.pdf; open and inspect.

yes.description: Complete rendered PDF with motivation, methodology, results, analysis, conclusion.

no.description: PDF absent, empty, or placeholder.

leaves.question: Does proposal/logs/ exist with non-empty per-run records?
leaves.evidence: ls proposal/logs/; inspect a sample of files for hyperparameters, seeds, metrics, timestamps.

yes.description: Logs directory exists with per-run records.

no.description: Logs absent or essentially empty.

leaves.question: Are reimplemented quadratic SNAP baseline runs logged on tantalum at the full CV protocol (5% increments, 10 draws per fraction)?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/ for the reimplemented quadratic SNAP CV sweep on tantalum.

yes.description: Reimplemented quadratic SNAP CV sweep is logged completely on tantalum.

no.description: Reimplemented quadratic SNAP runs absent or substantively incomplete.

leaves.question: Are learned-descriptor model runs logged at the full CV protocol (5% increments, 10 draws per fraction) on tantalum and on at least one transfer material?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/ for the proposed-method CV sweep across materials.

yes.description: Learned-descriptor runs logged completely on Ta and at least one transfer material.

no.description: Proposed-method runs absent or substantively incomplete.

leaves.question: Is the cross-validation sweep on tantalum complete at the paper's strict protocol (19 held-out fractions, 5% to 95% in 5% increments, 10 random draws per fraction, plus the full-data endpoint) for both reimplemented quadratic SNAP and the learned descriptor?
leaves.evidence: proposal/logs/ run records, cross-checked against the main paper's Figure 5 reproduction.

yes.description: All 19 held-out fractions × 10 draws = 190 runs per method (plus the full-data fit) are present in the logs.

no.description: Fewer fractions, fewer draws, or coverage gaps.

leaves.question: Is proposal/logs/paper_reference.md (or equivalent) present, listing every paper-as-reported quadratic SNAP value with its specific Wood & Thompson 2018 source location (Table SI / Table SII / Figure N)?
leaves.evidence: Filesystem check; inspect contents for specific table/figure citations.

yes.description: Audit trail for paper-as-reported values is present and specific.

no.description: No audit trail — paper-as-reported numbers cannot be verified against the source.

leaves.question: Is the main results table present in the paper, labeled tab:main_results, with two-baseline rows (paper-as-reported quadratic SNAP + reimplemented quadratic SNAP) and learned-descriptor rows per material?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex search for \label{tab:main_results}.

yes.description: Table present with two-baseline structure and per-material learned-descriptor entries.

no.description: Table absent, or missing two-baseline rows, or missing per-material entries.

leaves.question: Are data-efficiency curves present for all training groups (energy MAE vs. training fraction included, mean ± std across 10 draws, for both reimplemented quadratic SNAP and the learned descriptor), including the slow-converging groups (GSF, Liquid, Surface) plotted following paper Figure 5's structure with the learned-descriptor overlay?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex figures; cross-reference with paper.md Figure 5.

yes.description: Per-group curves present (including the slow-converging GSF, Liquid, and Surface groups) with both methods, error bands, and 5% increments.

no.description: Curve absent, missing one method, missing error bands, or coarser-than-5% sweep.

leaves.question: Are per-group data-efficiency curves present for all 12 training groups, plus an equal-weight all-groups aggregate curve?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex supporting figures or appendix.

yes.description: Per-group curves cover all 12 groups and an equal-weight aggregate is reported.

no.description: Fewer than all 12 groups covered, or no aggregate reported.

leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex figures showing per-transfer-material CV sweeps.

yes.description: At least one transfer-material curve is present at the strict protocol.

no.description: No transfer-material curve, or the curve is at a looser protocol than tantalum.

yes.description: All three tests are logged with the specified sample counts.

no.description: One or more tests missing, or sample counts below spec.

no.description: Timing logs absent or only one method timed.

method_specification.title: Learned-descriptor specification
method_specification.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: Is the learned-descriptor architecture and training procedure fully stated in Methodology before any empirical results are described?
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex section ordering.

yes.description: Methodology fully specifies the descriptor before Results.

no.description: Descriptor specification appears within or after Results.

leaves.question: Is the descriptor architecture specified completely enough that a domain expert could reimplement it from the paper alone?
leaves.evidence: Methodology section: architecture diagram or equations, layer specifications, output dimension K', input representation, training loss, regularization.

tiers.name: complete
tiers.description: Architecture is fully specified: layer types and sizes, activations, output dimension, cutoff radius, training objective, regularization. A reader could reimplement without the code.

tiers.name: partial
tiers.description: Major architectural choices stated but some details (e.g., exact layer sizes, training hyperparameters) require consulting the code.

tiers.name: qualitative_only
tiers.description: Architecture is described in prose without specific layer / dimension / hyperparameter content.

leaves.question: Are the proposed method's required hyperparameters listed with concrete values sufficiently completely to reproduce the scientific protocol? Whether quoted values contradict executed values is assessed only in integrity.
leaves.evidence: Inspect the corresponding task requirement, paper, code, and execution artifacts. Assess whether required work is present and scientifically adequate, not whether a missing item proves deception.

satisfied.description: The applicable scientific/documentation requirement is satisfied.
satisfied.criteria: Affirmatively establish every applicable component of the question from the submitted evidence and the task. Use the task's actual numerical thresholds and allowed alternatives; absence of a demonstrated problem is not sufficient.

not_satisfied.description: Required work is missing, incomplete, or scientifically noncompliant; describe the specific shortfall.

insufficient_evidence.description: The submitted evidence cannot establish whether the applicable scientific requirement is satisfied. This is not a pass and is not an integrity finding.

not_applicable.description: The task makes this conditional/optional and its antecedent is absent; explain the task-supported reason. An unconditional requirement cannot be waived this way.

leaves.question: Are the rotation / translation / permutation invariance properties of the descriptor stated explicitly in Methodology — and is the mechanism by which they hold (or fail to hold) named?
leaves.evidence: Methodology section discussion of invariances.

tiers.name: by_construction
tiers.description: The descriptor's invariances are stated and shown to hold architecturally (e.g., via equivariant layers, symmetry-respecting pooling). Drift is expected at machine precision.

tiers.name: via_data_augmentation
tiers.description: The descriptor is not architecturally invariant; invariances are encouraged via data augmentation during training. The augmentation strategy is stated, and the expected residual drift is discussed.

tiers.name: not_enforced_acknowledged
tiers.description: The descriptor is not invariant and the paper acknowledges this, treating measured drift as a property to characterize rather than eliminate.

tiers.name: claimed_but_not_substantiated
tiers.description: Paper claims invariance without substantiating the mechanism — neither architecture nor augmentation is shown to enforce it.

leaves.question: Does the proposed method preserve the SNAP-style energy form (linear + quadratic on the learned descriptor, isolated atom has zero energy, analytic-gradient forces) as required by the held-fixed clause?
leaves.evidence: Methodology equations; cross-check against the code.

yes.description: Energy form preserved: linear + quadratic on descriptors, isolated-atom energy exactly zero (via bzeroflag=1 or equivalent isolated-atom descriptor-value subtraction), forces backpropagated through descriptor.

no.description: Energy form differs (e.g., end-to-end NN energy, dropped quadratic terms, free constant added).

leaves.question: Is the descriptor's motivation grounded in the published MLIP / physics / chemistry / applied mathematics literature?
leaves.evidence: Methodology and Related Work; bibliography.

tiers.name: substantive
tiers.description: Method positioned against relevant published work (learned descriptors, MLIP, or the pertinent physics / chemistry / applied-mathematics literature, including post-2018 developments) with specific citations and substantive comparison.

tiers.name: moderate
tiers.description: Some literature referenced; positioning is shallow or uneven.

tiers.name: thin
tiers.description: Few citations; descriptor presented as if standalone.

tiers.name: absent
tiers.description: No engagement with the relevant literature.

leaves.question: How close is the reimplemented quadratic SNAP on tantalum to the paper-as-reported numbers (Table SII, J_max=4: δE = 0.00898 eV/atom; J_max=5: δE = 0.00163 eV/atom)?

tiers.name: close_match
tiers.description: Reimplemented δE matches paper-as-reported within ~20% on the headline (e.g., 0.007–0.011 eV/atom for J_max=4).

tiers.name: modest_under_convergence
tiers.description: Reimplemented δE is modestly off paper-as-reported (e.g., 20–50% higher).

tiers.name: substantial_under_convergence
tiers.description: Reimplemented δE is substantially off paper-as-reported (2–3× higher), suggesting protocol gaps or weight-tuning differences.

tiers.name: no_match
tiers.description: Reimplemented δE is catastrophically off paper-as-reported (>3× higher) or qualitatively different from paper findings, suggesting a fundamentally broken FitSNAP run rather than honest under-convergence.

data_efficiency.title: Data efficiency vs. reimplemented quadratic SNAP
data_efficiency.purpose: Assess the task's applicable scientific or completeness requirements for this cluster; integrity is assessed separately.

leaves.question: On the ta material, classify the data efficiency of the learned descriptor against reimplemented quadratic SNAP based on the CV sweep curves. Compute: the smallest training fraction F* at which the learned descriptor's prediction δE (mean over 10 draws) reaches reimplemented quadratic SNAP's full-data prediction δE. For the classification: on tantalum, use the low-symmetry / slow-converging subset (GSF, Liquid, Surface) — the discriminating groups where the bar has teeth, since the high-symmetry groups reach full accuracy at tiny data fractions for both methods. On the transfer materials (Mo, Nb, Re), whose datasets have a different group structure (temperature-batched MD trajectories, not the tantalum thermodynamic groups), use the equal-weight all-groups aggregate (or the slow-converging analogue where the transfer dataset's own group structure permits). The tantalum equal-weight all-12-group aggregate outcome is reported and scored separately (see data_efficiency_breadth.equal_weight_aggregate_efficiency).
leaves.evidence: proposal/report.tex per-material data-efficiency curves; cross-check with proposal/logs/ per-fraction means.

tiers.name: substantial
tiers.description: Learned descriptor reaches baseline's full-data δE at ≤ 50% training data. Sample-efficiency ratio ≥ 2×.

tiers.name: modest
tiers.description: Learned descriptor reaches baseline's full-data δE at 50%–80% training data. Sample-efficiency ratio in [1.25×, 2×).

tiers.name: matches
tiers.description: Learned descriptor reaches baseline's full-data δE at 80%–95% training data. No meaningful sample-efficiency advantage.

tiers.name: no_advantage
tiers.description: Learned descriptor reaches baseline's full-data δE only near 95–100% training data.

tiers.name: regression
tiers.description: Learned descriptor does not reach baseline's full-data δE on the CV sweep, or requires more training data than the baseline to do so.

tiers.name: not_evaluated
tiers.description: Material ta was not evaluated in the submission.

data_efficiency_breadth.title: Data-efficiency reporting breadth

leaves.question: How well do the data-efficiency curves reproduce paper Figure 5's structure (5% increments, 10 draws, mean ± std bands, both training error and prediction error reported) across the reported groups, especially the slow-converging groups (GSF, Liquid, Surface)?

assessment_policy.scope: Completeness and scientific quality only: required artifacts, executed experimental coverage, reproducible methodology, mathematical/statistical validity, performance targets, and task-required analysis/writing.
assessment_policy.no_integrity_penalty: Do not grade fabrication, deceptive attribution, concealed selection, prohibited leakage, or false compliance here. Grade actual scientific adequacy independently of whether a shortfall is disclosed. Integrity evidence is assessed only in integrity_check_rubric.json.
assessment_policy.authoritative_task: The accompanying unchanged task specification controls required versus optional work and permitted exceptions. A qualitative quality tier is not authority to introduce a new experiment, resource limit, or numerical minimum absent from the task.
assessment_policy.conditional_nodes: Respect applicability. Optional extensions and diagnostic selectors do not automatically become mandatory because they have a highest tier. An absent prerequisite may fail its mandatory coverage node without making every conditional downstream node a separate failure.
assessment_policy.inference: Insufficient scientific support is not itself dishonesty. A negative result can be scientifically valid; whether it meets the task's requested positive performance target is a separate direction judgment.
